newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says BS-4b broadcast satellite to be digital.
newsitem.headline: Japan says BS-4b broadcast satellite to be digital.

text.p: Japan's Posts and Telecommunications Ministry said on Friday that BS-4b, Japan's next broadcast satellite due to be launched in 2000, would employ digital broadcasting technology.
It said the decision would be formalised in May after discussions in the ministry's Radio Wave Council.

Japan had been due to decide on the technology to be used in BS-4b by May 1996. But the ministry delayed the decision by a year as Japanese electronics firms and broadcasters asked it to expand the number of analogue satellite broadcasting channels after 2000.
Electronics firms had said moves toward digital could jeopardise fledgling sales of their analogue advanced television system called Hi-Vision, which has cost more than 300 billion yen to develop.

Viewers with Hi-Vision television sets and subscribers to Japan Public Broadcasting Company's analogue broadcasts would be able to see digital programmes by buying digital adapters, the ministry said.

BS-4b will have four transponders, and will be able to send at least eight programmes simultaneously using digital technology, as opposed to four if analogue technology were to be used, the ministry said.
